claim_text: If a Nigerian company declares a dividend out of profits on which no tax is payable because there are no total profits, the company paying the dividend is charged to tax.
The same applies where total profits are less than the dividend declared, whether or not the recipient is a Nigerian company.

The company is charged at the rate prescribed in section 56 of the Act, as if the dividend were the company's total profits for the year of assessment to which the accounts, out of which the dividend is declared, relate.
This rule does not apply to dividends declared out of retained earnings, to the extent the profits or gains in them have been taxed under the Act.
It also does not apply to dividends declared out of profits or gains that are exempt from income tax by the Act, or to franked investment income as provided in the Act.

It also does not apply to distributions by a real estate investment company to its shareholders from rental income and dividend income received on behalf of those shareholders, whether paid out of profits of the year of declaration or of previous reporting periods.

Section 21 also bars a deduction for any tax or penalty borne on behalf of another person.

claim_text: A non-resident person who makes taxable supplies to Nigeria must register for tax and include VAT on its invoice for all taxable supplies.

Where a non-resident makes taxable supplies from outside Nigeria to persons in Nigeria, the taxable person in Nigeria to whom the supply is made must withhold the VAT due on the supply and remit it to the Service.
The Service may, by notice, appoint any person, including a non-resident supplier, to collect the VAT and remit it to the Service.

If such an appointed person has made the supply to a taxable person in Nigeria, the Nigerian taxable person has no obligation to withhold the VAT, unless the appointed person has failed to collect it.
A non-resident supplier may appoint a representative to handle its VAT compliance.
The Service may direct a taxable person who is issued an invoice on which VAT is not included to self-account for the VAT payable and remit it to the Service.

VAT that is collected, withheld or self-accounted under section 155 must be remitted on or before the 14th day of the month immediately following the month of the transaction, or as the Service prescribes.

The remittance must come with a schedule showing the name, Tax ID and address of the contractor or supplier, invoice number, gross amount of invoice, amount of the VAT and the month to which the return relates.
A person who must collect VAT must keep proper records and make returns and remittances, and the compliance rules apply to that person as though it were the taxable person.
A foreign company is defined as a company other than a Nigerian company, and in the Nigeria Tax Act it also includes a non-resident company.

claim_text: If the relevant tax authority finds or thinks that a taxable person was not assessed, or was assessed at too little, it may assess the right amount or the additional amount within six years of the assessment.
The six-year limit does not stop the tax authority from continuing a tax audit and raising an additional assessment, if the audit began before the six years ended.

So the disputed part of the tax is not collected while the objection is pending, but the undisputed part remains payable.
